inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 Annual Report, statement of changes in equity line 1811 (equity-settled share-based payments 4,223k); the Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation (note 5, line 2153) cites 'equity-based compensation and associated expenses of $4.2 million' - same figure, so no separate equity-award tax line is added. Filing units are $'000; converted to millions.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-23T06:10:04Z (ASX regular close, ex the 8.0c final dividend whose record date was 11 Sep 2026)
inputs.share_count_basis: 94,864,551 fully paid ordinary shares on issue at 30 June 2026 (AR note 3.3a, line 3604) plus 1,852,459 dilutive Performance Rights and Options from the diluted-EPS table (line 3757) = 96.72m. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would double-charge it. The count is being funded: $20.2m of buybacks in FY26 (5.16m shares, 5.2% of capital) under a 10% authorisation that runs to May 2027, so the flat count is a paid-for convention, not a modelling gift. A further 3.09m unvested Rights and 0.31m Options exist beyond the treasury-stock dilution; their cost is the forward SBC charge.
inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD-denominated flows discounted at an AUD-built rate: Australian 10-year government bond ~4.3%, equity risk premium 5.5%, beta ~1.25 for a small-cap online retailer with a thin equity base => cost of equity ~11.2%; no bank debt (the $30m facility was drawn and repaid intra-year and is undrawn at 30 June 2026), so WACC = cost of equity, rounded to 11.0%. One WACC across all three scenarios: structural competition, Mighty Ape execution and the thin balance sheet are charged in the bear-scenario flows and its 30% weight, not stacked as a second premium on the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: the full IFRS-16 lease payment (principal + interest, $8.8m FY26 = 1.72% of revenue) is deducted inside the flows via lease_cost_pct_path, lease liabilities ($17.4m) are excluded from net debt, and da_pct_path is D&A EX right-of-use depreciation (FY26: 16.080 total less 7.905 ROU depreciation = 8.175, i.e. 1.60% of revenue: 0.524 PP&E depreciation + 7.651 amortisation of software and acquired Mighty Ape intangibles). The Adjusted EBITDA margin path is therefore the post-IFRS-16 figure the company reports (FY26 $41.8m, 8.2%), with the lease charge taken separately below it.
inputs.nci_treatment: None - all subsidiaries wholly owned; no non-controlling interests.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon (margin still ramping toward the guided 8-12% band at year 5), routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical: consumer' with the adaptations file applied (AUD WACC, single lease treatment, no NCI, interest income stripped with cash in the bridge). FY0 = FY2026 (year ended 30 June 2026, reported 24 Aug 2026). Owner FCF FY26 = reported FCF 38.349 - SBC 4.223 - interest income 0.804 - lease cash 8.794 = 24.53 (4.8% of revenue). Interest income is stripped even though net cash is ~0.95x the FCF base, because the cash is added to EV in the bridge and the $0.8m is immaterial either way. Adjusted EBITDA (pre-SBC, post-IFRS-16, ex unrealised FX and the $0.3m marketing-compliance provision) is the margin anchor: FY24 40.0, FY25 36.8, FY26 41.8. Do NOT read FY25 net income (-39.5m, $46.3m Mighty Ape goodwill impairment) or FY24 net income (0.08m, $21.1m deferred-tax-asset write-down) as run-rate: pretax profit before those items was ~$13m and ~$21m. SBC ran $20-31m/yr in FY21-23 (founder options plus Mighty Ape earn-out accruals) and a further $17.6m of options were cash-settled in FY24; those are done - the forward SBC charge is anchored to the FY26 actual (0.83% of revenue). Buybacks are value-neutral here (they fund the flat count); the FY26 equity fall from $53.9m to $34.4m is $33.2m of capital returned, not operating losses. Equity bridge deducts the declared 8.0c final dividend (~$7.6m) because the price is ex-dividend but the cash is still on the 30 June balance sheet.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Forward segment mix, not a historical CAGR: Kogan.com (83% of revenue) grew 18% in FY26 while Mighty Ape (17%) shrank 30% in a deliberate inventory reset that management says is complete; blended year-1-to-3 base path of 7/6/5% averages ~5-6%. Every historical CAGR here describes the FY21 COVID peak ($780.7m) and the FY22-23 inventory unwind, not the current business.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-28% 5yr, -41% 3yr) is not an operating signal: $58.9m of buybacks and $31.9m of dividends since FY23 plus the $46.3m FY25 goodwill impairment shrank book equity from $167.7m to $34.4m while the group stayed net cash. Owner-FCF 3yr CAGR (-2.6%) is 14pp above the reported-FCF CAGR (-16.9%) because the FY23 base was inflated by an inventory unwind AND by $31.3m of SBC that has since collapsed to $4.2m - the SBC-adjusted series is the flatter, truer one here. EPS 5yr CAGR (+29.7%) compounds from a $0.03 FY21 base and is meaningless; 3yr is null (negative FY23 base).
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - interest income - lease principal; lease interest only available and deducted for FY25-26): FY20 34.8, FY21 -91.4, FY22 19.4, FY23 26.6, FY24 11.5 (before the $17.6m cash settlement of options, after which it is -6.1), FY25 21.0, FY26 24.5. Cash tax paid FY24-26 (2.7, 4.6, 4.0) ran at 13-25% of pretax profit because of carried-forward tax losses; the remaining tax-loss DTA is $5.4m at 30 June 2026 (down from $10.6m), so the shelter is nearly exhausted.

base.growth_rationale: FY27 +7%: Kogan.com ~+11% (FY26 +18% off a soft FY25, decelerating as Temu/Shein reach grows) offset by Mighty Ape roughly flat after its 30% reset. Fades to 2.5% nominal by year 9 - Australian online retail grows mid-single digits but Kogan's share is slipping.
base.margin_rationale: Adjusted EBITDA margin 8.2% FY26 -> 10.5% mature, i.e. inside management's 8-12% medium-term band but 1.5pp short of the 12% they are 'progressing toward'; that haircut is the market's 15% results-day skepticism made explicit. Driver is Platform-based Sales mix (61% of gross profit, 50-55% adjusted margin) plus Mighty Ape returning to full-year positive Adjusted EBITDA in FY27 as guided.
base.tax_rationale: Cash tax 22% FY27 (FY26 paid 21% of pretax) ramping to the 30% Australian statutory rate by FY29 as the $5.4m tax-loss DTA is used up; NZ losses at Mighty Ape are unrecognised and give no shelter.
base.capex_da_rationale: Capex 0.7% of revenue in FY26 is below the 1.2-1.6% of FY18-20; normalised up to 1.2% (platform re-investment, warehouse fit-outs). D&A ex-ROU (1.6% FY26) converges down to capex as the acquired Mighty Ape brand/customer intangibles finish amortising.
base.wc_rationale: Mildly negative-working-capital business (payables $95m vs inventory + receivables ~$60m; deferred subscription income $23m growing +16%): 5% capture on the revenue increase, positive because platform/subscription growth funds itself while Products growth needs some inventory.

bull.rationale: Management's own 12% Adjusted EBITDA margin reached in year 5 and overshot to 13% as Platform-based Sales pass 70% of gross profit; Mighty Ape recovers to its pre-migration ~NZ$130m and the Marketplace/PRIMATE/Mighty Mobile lines scale; lease intensity falls as inventory-light mix needs less warehouse. Still capped at 14x terminal FCF - no re-rating to compounder multiples is assumed.

bear.rationale: Temu/Shein/Amazon take the value-shopper: Kogan.com growth stalls and the group shrinks ~6% over FY28-29 as Mighty Ape fails to hold FY27 profitability; Products margin is squeezed back toward FY25 levels and Adjusted EBITDA margin falls to 6% (below the guided band) before stabilising at 6.5%; fixed lease cost rises as a share of a smaller revenue base. The company remains cash-generative (no going-concern outcome - net cash, no debt) but is a low-growth, sub-scale local marketplace: 12x terminal cap, 1.5% terminal growth.

scenario_narratives.base: Kogan.com keeps compounding Platform-based Sales (Marketplace, Kogan FIRST, Verticals, Advertising - 61% of FY26 gross profit at 50-55% margin) at high single digits while Products grows slowly at a ~21% gross margin; Mighty Ape, reset by 30% in FY26, is flat in FY27 and delivers the guided full-year positive Adjusted EBITDA. Group revenue grows 7% in FY27 decelerating to 2.5% by FY35; Adjusted EBITDA margin rises from 8.2% to 10.5% - inside the guided 8-12% band but short of the 12% ambition, because Temu and Shein continue to take share of Australian value shoppers and marketing intensity (15.7% of revenue in FY26) does not fall. Cash tax normalises to 30% by FY29 as the last $5.4m of tax-loss shelter is consumed. Buybacks continue to fund a flat share count.
scenario_narratives.bull: The mix-shift thesis fully plays out: Platform-based Sales pass 70% of gross profit, AI-driven cost-out (customer care automated from March 2026) drops marketing and people cost as a share of revenue, and Mighty Ape recovers to pre-migration scale with PRIMATE and Mighty Mobile scaling off their low base. Group revenue grows 10% in FY27 fading to 3%, and the Adjusted EBITDA margin hits management's 12% target in FY31 and 13% by FY33. Being the last Australian-owned marketplace of scale becomes an asset - local sellers who cannot get onto Amazon consolidate on Kogan - and a takeover by a strategic buyer becomes plausible, though no control premium is modelled.
scenario_narratives.bear: The structural squeeze wins. Amazon, Temu and Shein approach a third of Australian online retail; Kogan's shopper reach keeps falling and the company has to choose between losing volume or discounting into negative Products margin. Revenue is flat in FY27 and contracts through FY29; Mighty Ape does not sustain profitability and needs a second reset; Adjusted EBITDA margin falls to 6%, below the guided band. The business stays cash-positive and debt-free so there is no solvency event, but the thin $34m equity base and NTA of $0.04/share mean any further impairment or restatement (FY25 Mighty Ape accruals were restated in the FY26 report) removes the buyback capacity that currently supports the share price.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 30%: the competitive threat is structural rather than cyclical (Catch and MyDeal have already closed; Kogan's shopper share fell ~6pp in a year), Mighty Ape's turnaround is one positive quarter old and its subsidiary controls produced a restatement, and the equity base is too thin to absorb another shock without cutting the capital return. Bull cut to 20% because it requires three independent things - Mighty Ape recovery, margin to 12%+, and growth re-acceleration against better-capitalised rivals - to go right together. Base 50%: management's guided band, haircut.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Kogan is valued as a cash-generative, debt-free, low-capital online retailer whose worth is the owner FCF from its platform businesses - not its book value, which is now nearly meaningless. The FY25 loss and the collapse of equity from $180m (FY21) to $34m (FY26) are two different stories that must not be blended: the FY25 loss was a non-cash $46.3m goodwill write-off on Mighty Ape (EBITDA before impairment was positive $31.7m), and the equity erosion since FY23 is overwhelmingly $59m of buybacks and $32m of dividends returned to shareholders from a net-cash balance sheet - capital returns, not operating losses. Likewise FY24's near-zero net income was a $21.1m deferred-tax-asset write-down on $21m of pretax profit. The model therefore anchors on Adjusted EBITDA (FY24-26: 40.0 / 36.8 / 41.8), builds owner FCF from components with leases charged as an operating cost, SBC expensed at its post-founder-option run-rate (0.8% of revenue, not the FY21-23 $20-31m years), interest income stripped, and cash tax ramped to 30% as the tax-loss shelter runs out. Risk is charged in the flows and the scenario weights (30% bear), not through a stacked WACC premium. The terminal cap of 14x owner FCF (12x in the bear) reflects a structurally pressured local marketplace, not a compounder.
key_risks_to_valuation: Structural share loss to Amazon/Temu/Shein: the bear case (margin to 6%, revenue contracting FY28-29) carries 30% weight and is the main reason weighted IV sits close to the price rather than above it
Mighty Ape: only one positive quarter of Adjusted EBITDA (Q4 FY26, $0.4m) and a restated FY25 balance sheet; a second failed year would push the group toward the bear path
Margin-guidance risk: the base assumes 10.5% mature Adjusted EBITDA margin against 8.2% actual and a 12% target - each 1pp of mature margin is worth roughly $0.45-0.55/share
Thin equity ($34.4m, NTA $0.04/share): no solvency risk while net cash, but a further impairment or provision would likely end the buyback that keeps the share count flat
Cash tax: FY26 paid only 21% of pretax; the model ramps to 30% by FY29 - if losses are recognised or R&D incentives persist the base is conservative, if the DTA is written down again the reverse
Terminal value share: with a 14x cap and 11% WACC, roughly 45-50% of base EV sits in the terminal; a 1pp change in WACC moves base IV by about 10%
